**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Religious Studies 2 (0785), Paper 2: The Old Testament/Islam and African Traditional Religious Beliefs and Practices. ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY. All questions carry equal marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Les références bibliques citées (Genèse 12, 15, 17, 25, 27-29, 32-33, 37, 50 ; Exode 19-20, 24, 32, 34 ; 1 Samuel 1-3, 7-13, 15-16, 22, 28, 31 ; Jérémie 31 ; Genèse 22) sont des passages classiques ; les numéros de versets précis ne sont donnés que pour des textes très connus. Aucune référence n'est inventée.

Section Islam (Q7-12) : exposé du fiqh sunnite courant ; les écoles juridiques divergent sur plusieurs points de la Q7 (injections, gouttes pour les yeux, inhalateurs, émission volontaire sans rapport sexuel, tabac) et le corrigé le dit. Q9 : l'identité du fils sacrifié (Ismaël selon la tradition musulmane majoritaire, non nommé par le Coran) est présentée prudemment ; la date de l'institution de la fête est donnée « selon la tradition ». Q10 : positions des savants courants, sans attribution à un texte précis au-delà de Coran 5:32, 2:190 et 2:256, versets très connus. Q11 : l'occasion de la révélation de la sourate 109 est rapportée « selon la tradition islamique » ; renvois à 2:256, 60:8 et 6:108 (versets bien établis). Q12 : l'imamat chiite est mentionné de façon descriptive (chiisme duodécimain), sans jugement.

Section ATR (Q13-18) : généralités tirées des auteurs classiques du programme (Mbiti en particulier : « I am because we are... », « living-dead ») ; les croyances varient selon les peuples et le corrigé le dit. Exemples cités avec prudence : Obatala et Olodumare chez les Yoruba (Q13), « chi » chez les Igbo (Q15). Aucune tradition locale camerounaise n'est inventée.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Comment on the importance of the rituals of death celebrations in ATR.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** In ATR death is not the end of existence but a passage from the world of the living to the world of the spirits and the ancestors. Death and burial rites are therefore among the most important rituals of the community. They differ in detail among peoples, so the points below are general.

**1. They ensure a proper passage to the spirit world.** The correct performance of the rites (washing and dressing the body, burial in the right place with the proper words and gifts) is believed to help the dead person to join the ancestors. A person who is denied proper rites, or who dies in disgrace or far from home, may wander as a restless spirit and trouble the living.

**2. They make a person an ancestor.** A person who has lived a good life and has descendants, and who is given a full funeral, is eventually honoured as an ancestor, who becomes a protector of the family and an intermediary with God. Second funerals or memorial rites, held some time after burial, mark this change.

**3. They express respect and love.** The size of the ceremony, with feasting, music, drumming, dancing and sometimes sacrifice, shows the honour given to the deceased, especially to elders, chiefs and old persons, who are given elaborate funerals.

**4. They bring the community together.** Relatives and neighbours come from afar, bring gifts, share food and spend days together. This strengthens solidarity and shows that the dead and the living belong to one family.

**5. They console the bereaved.** Mourning, wailing, songs and the presence of others help the family express grief and receive support. Rules for widows and widowers (dress, seclusion, cleansing) mark the stages of mourning, and a special rite ends the period.

**6. They purify and protect the living.** Death is considered ritually dangerous, so purification of the mourners and the house, shaving of hair, and sacrifices to avert further misfortune are performed. Where death is thought to have come from sorcery, rites and divination may be used to find the cause.

**7. They have social and legal functions.** The funeral is the time to announce the successor, share the inheritance and settle debts, to renew family bonds and to teach the young their duties.

**8. They affirm belief in life after death.** Food, drink, clothes, tools or other objects are sometimes put in the grave or poured out as libation, showing that the dead still need and share things, and that the departed remain part of the family.

**Assessment.** Today funerals are changing under Christian and Muslim influence, costs and urban life. Some customs are criticised for expense or for harsh treatment of widows. Yet the rites remain important for the community's identity.

**Conclusion.** Death rituals in ATR are important because they assure the safe passage of the dead to the ancestors, console and cleanse the living, reunite the community and express belief in the continuity of life.
